title: Vector-bundle purity
statement:
In the finite-coefficient part of the current purity conventions ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting), put $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ with $n\geq1$. The integral, rational and algebraically closed versions are the separate coefficient transports of the blueprint transport section. In the ordinary-etale realization of the finite constructible category,
let $\pi:E\to B$ be a vector bundle of constant rank $r$ with zero
section $z$ [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. For every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(B,\Lambda)$ there is a
canonical isomorphism

$$
R\pi^!K\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;L\pi^*K(r)[2r],
$$

compatible with base change, with direct sums of vector bundles, and
with the adjunctions; in particular

$$
\omega_\pi=R\pi^!\Lambda_B\;\cong\;\Lambda_E(r)[2r],
$$

and the identification is compatible with the finite reduction of the
coefficients.

Write gamma_{pi,K}=alpha_{pi,K}^{-1} for the adjoint of the actual integration trace after inverse projection. Every compatibility below concerns this same independently integration-normalized family.

For an arbitrary base change g:B'→B and its pullback bundle pi':E'→B', let e:g'^*Rpi^!→Rpi'^!g^* be the exceptional exchange (the mate of the inverse compact-support exchange) and a the tensor/pullback/Tate associator. On K in D^b_ctf(B,A), e is invertible and g'^*(gamma_{pi,K}) ≫ e_K = a_K ≫ gamma_{pi',g^*K}.

For F⊕G of ranks r,s use the canonical projections q:E(F⊕G)→E(G), j:E(F⊕G)→E(F), p:E(G)→B, and h=pq. Let c:R h^!≈R q^!R p^! be the right-adjoint mate of the compact-support compositor formed through an actual compactification triangle. With gamma_q obtained by base change of the first bundle's unit orientation and the dualizing tensor map, gamma_h equals a_{r,s} ≫ (1 tensor q^*gamma_p) ≫ gamma_q ≫ c^{-1}, the ordered Step-5 composite.

For each 1≤m≤n use the quotient A_{E,n}→A_{E,m} and its derived scalar tensor Q [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Form q_scalar:Q_B Rpi_{!,n}≈Rpi_{!,m}Q_E from the canonical open-extension/proper-direct-image coefficient comparison. Let b_{n,m} be the exceptional adjoint of q_scalar^{-1} ≫ Q_B(epsilon_n). Let a_scalar be the scalar tensor/pullback/Tate comparison, whose ordinary line comparison sends a tensor z to phi(a) tensor z. Then Q_E(gamma_{pi,K}) ≫ b_{n,m,K} = a_scalar,K ≫ gamma_{pi,Q_B K}, with both vertical maps invertible, including the component K=the coefficient-unit OBJECT.

The normalization and the three displayed predicates are defined in [def-pur-vector-purity-normalization], [def-pur-vector-purity-base-change], [def-pur-vector-purity-direct-sum], [def-pur-vector-purity-finite-reduction].

proof.text:
Work with $A=A_{E,n}$ on the ordinary etale site, as the current statement requires. The base and the bundle have the Noetherian and constant-rank meaning of [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]; $\ell$ is invertible by [def-pur-conventions]. The construction [def-amb-vector-integration] supplies a compactification, the ordinary Tate sheaf, and the actual trace $t_\pi:R\pi_!A_E(r)[2r]\to A_B$. Let $W=A_E(r)[2r]$. The theorem [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity] states that the canonical projection is invertible and that the transpose of
$$c_{\pi,K}=(1_K\otimes t_\pi)\circ P_{\pi;K,W}^{-1}:R\pi_!(\pi^*K\otimes W)\to K$$
is an isomorphism $\gamma_{\pi,K}:\pi^*K\otimes W\to\pi^\times K$, for every ordinary etale complex $K$. Restrict to the bounded constructible finite-Tor category and set $\alpha_{\pi,K}=\gamma_{\pi,K}^{-1}$. Tensor symmetry identifies the displayed source with the statement's ordered convention. This is exactly the integration-normalized family of [def-pur-vector-purity-normalization], including its coefficient-unit component; no pro-etale witness or higher coefficient passage is needed in this finite ordinary-etale assertion.

source.place: paragraph 1: finite ordinary-etale integration and its transpose

proof.text: The normalization gives $\varepsilon_K R\pi_!(\gamma_{\pi,K})=c_{\pi,K}$, by the transpose formula [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. A different natural family with this same equation has equal components because the adjunction Hom map is injective. Write $G_0K=\pi^*K(r)[2r]$. The adjunction carried through $\gamma:G_0\cong\pi^\times$ has counit $\varepsilon_0=\varepsilon\circ R\pi_!\gamma$ and unit $\eta_{0,M}=\gamma_{R\pi_!M}^{-1}\circ\eta_M$. Substitution in each triangle identity, followed by naturality of $\gamma$ and cancellation of $\gamma^{-1}\gamma$, gives the identity. Thus the identification preserves the specified units and counits and proves compatibility with adjunctions, rather than asserting only an isomorphism of objects.

source.place: paragraph 1: compatibility with the actual adjunction and counit

proof.text: For the base-change square of [def-pur-vector-purity-base-change], let $C:g^*R\pi_!\cong R\pi'_!g'^*$ be compact-support exchange. It exists with its proper/open normalization by [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. On every trivializing open and its pullback, the trace of [def-amb-vector-integration] is the affine-space counit and [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] gives $t_{\pi'} C_W=g^*t_\pi$. Both source and target have cohomology only in degree zero, since the source is locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf by that affine-space trace. The gluing and equality assertion [lem-pur-degree-zero-derived-map-gluing] therefore makes this equality global. Frame changes give the same trace by the actual equality $t_{p_r}\rho_G=t_{p_r}$ of [lem-amb-linear-trace-invariance]. This applies on Noetherian overlaps, without requiring overlaps to be affine. Pullback bases are Noetherian as required by the stated base-change predicate.

source.place: paragraph 2: base change and descent of the integration trace

proof.text:
Apply [lem-asd-compact-projection-exchange] to $\pi$, its pulled-back compactification, $K$ and $W$. It says precisely that compact-support projection commutes with this arbitrary base change. Its inverse square and the trace equality of Step 3 identify the base-changed $c_{\pi,K}$ with $c_{\pi',g^*K}$. Define $e:g'^*\pi^\times K\to\pi'^\times g^*K$ by its transpose
$$R\pi'_!g'^*\pi^\times K\xrightarrow{C^{-1}}g^*R\pi_!\pi^\times K\xrightarrow{g^*\varepsilon_K}g^*K.$$
This is exactly the exceptional mate convention [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Naturality of $C$ and the equation $\varepsilon R\pi_!\gamma=c$ give equal transposes for $e_K g'^*\gamma_{\pi,K}$ and $\gamma_{\pi',g^*K}a_K$. Injectivity of transposition gives their equality. The source comparison $a_K$ is the canonical tensor/pullback comparison with the ordinary Tate identifications of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Since $a_K$ and both gamma maps are invertible, $e_K=\gamma_{\pi',g^*K}a_K(g'^*\gamma_{\pi,K})^{-1}$ is invertible. This proves the exact predicate of [def-pur-vector-purity-base-change] and its inverse-alpha square.

source.place: paragraph 2: transpose of the base-change trace equation

proof.text: Let $F,G$ have ranks $r,s$, and use $q:E(F\oplus G)\to E(G)$, $p:E(G)\to B$, $h=pq$ and $j$ as in [def-pur-vector-purity-direct-sum]. The relative symmetric-algebra description in [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section] identifies the sum bundle with $E(F)\times_BE(G)$: an algebra map from $\operatorname{Sym}(F\oplus G)$ is a pair of maps from its summands, so the relative spectra have this product universal property. Hence $q$ is the pulled-back rank-$r$ bundle. Use the composition comparison $\alpha:R p_!R q_!\cong Rh_!$ of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], formed through the compactification triangle in that statement. The ordered composite trace is $t_p\circ Rp_!(t_q)$ with projection and twist associators inserted. On simultaneous trivializations this is exactly the coordinate-tower counit of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] and [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Both it and $t_h$ have degree-zero source and target, so [lem-pur-degree-zero-derived-map-gluing] makes their local equality global. Reordering blocks preserves the trace by [lem-amb-linear-trace-invariance].

source.place: paragraph 2: ordered traces of direct sums and descent

proof.text:
The exact projection/composition identity [lem-amb-shriek-tensor-composition], with invertible projection maps from Step 1, permits tensoring the trace equality of Step 5 by $K$. Define $c:Rh^!\cong Rq^!Rp^!$ by the composite Hom bijection of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] under $\alpha$. Its counit is $\varepsilon_p\circ Rp_!(\varepsilon_q)\circ Rp_!Rq_!(c)$, inserting $\alpha^{-1}$ at the source. Transposing the tensored trace equality gives
$$\gamma_{h,K}=c_K^{-1}\circ\gamma_{q,Rp^!K}\circ(1\otimes q^*\gamma_{p,K})\circ a_{r,s,K}.$$
The Tate-power reassociation and shift comparison in $a_{r,s}$ are the ordinary tensor powers of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]; swapping shifts gives $(-1)^{(2r)(2s)}=1$. To identify the stipulated $\gamma_q$, let $\theta_{q,L}$ be the dualizing tensor map, the transpose of inverse projection followed by $1\otimes\varepsilon_{q,A}$. Naturality of projection in its source and $\varepsilon_{q,A}Rq_!\gamma_{q,A}=t_q$ show that $\theta_{q,L}(1\otimes\gamma_{q,A})$ has transpose $c_{q,L}$, hence equals $\gamma_{q,L}$ by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Step 4 at the unit identifies $\gamma_{q,A}$ with the pulled-back unit orientation of $F$. Thus the displayed formula is exactly [def-pur-vector-purity-direct-sum], for every compactification triangle, not a choice of unrelated comparison. Step 1 supplies these maps even on ambient inputs $Rp^!K$, so no additional finite-Tor preservation theorem is being assumed here.

source.place: paragraph 2: tensor-projected composite counits and their exceptional transposes

proof.text: Fix $1\le m\le n$, put $A'=A_{E,m}$, and let $Q_T=(-)\otimes_A^LA'$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Choose one $N=\ell^a$ killing both rings. Their ordinary Tate lines are $\mu_N\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}A$ and $\mu_N\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}A'$ and are flat rank-one sheaves [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. The balancing map $(a\otimes z)\otimes b\mapsto\phi(a)b\otimes z$, and its tensor powers, identify their scalar extensions, including power zero. For a flat degree-zero sheaf $M$, [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] computes $Q(M[0])$ by $M\otimes_AA'$ in degree zero. Use the actual normalized scalar adjunction of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. The unit roof in [lem-weil-pbc-scalar-extension-unit-triangles] is then $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Transposing this roof under the fixed scalar adjunction shows that the comparison $q_M$ of [def-pur-vector-purity-scalar-single] is exactly the same balancing map: its composite with the unit sends $x$ to $x\otimes1$, which determines its transpose. For $M=A$ this is multiplication $A\otimes_AA'\to A'$. Thus the scalar/single comparison at the unit and at rank zero is the stipulated one. With the K-flat tensorator [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and shift and pullback identifications, these give precisely the invertible source arrow $a_{\rm scalar}$ of [def-pur-vector-purity-finite-reduction]. No flatness of $A'$ over $A$ is used.

source.place: paragraph 2: canonical ordinary Tate scalar comparison, including rank zero

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-etale-compact-scalar-coherence] on the chosen compactification of $\pi$. It gives the actual isomorphism $q_{\pi,M}:Q_BR\pi_{!,A}M\to R\pi_{!,A'}Q_EM$, constructed from the proper scalar counit mate followed by the open scalar comparison; this is exactly $q_{\rm scalar}$ in [def-pur-vector-purity-finite-reduction]. In particular it is invertible at $M=R\pi_A^!K$, including $K=A_B$, without invoking a general smooth-purity theorem. Define $b_K$ to be the transpose of
$$R\pi_{!,A'}Q_ER\pi_A^!K\xrightarrow{q_{\pi,R\pi_A^!K}^{-1}}Q_BR\pi_{!,A}R\pi_A^!K\xrightarrow{Q_B\varepsilon_{A,K}}Q_BK.$$
The convention [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] makes this the published exceptional scalar mate. Its invertibility will follow from the normalized-gamma square, rather than from the false general principle that an invertible square always has invertible mate.

source.place: paragraph 2: construct the actual compact-support and exceptional scalar comparisons

proof.text: First check scalar compatibility of the projective-line trace. By [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer], its supported hyperplane class and its ordinary Chern class are derived scalar extensions of the same $\mathbf Z/N$ class; associativity of the K-flat scalar tensor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] gives $Q(h_A)=h_{A'}$ under the proper counit-mate comparison [lem-asd-proper-finite-coefficient-extension]. The unit component is preserved as well: by the defining transpose of that proper comparison, its composite with the scalar extension of the old inverse-image/direct-image unit has transpose the identity, hence is the new unit (apply the adjunction triangle identity). Therefore $q\,Q(b_A)=b_{A'}$ for the two-component decomposition of [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction], under Step 7's scalar source identifications. By [def-amb-p1-trace], $t_A=\operatorname{pr}_2b_A^{-1}$ and $t_{A'}=\operatorname{pr}_2b_{A'}^{-1}$. Functoriality preserves inverses and the finite direct-sum projection, so $t_{A'}q=Q(t_A)$. This proof uses the derived scalar extension of the Kummer class, not an assertion that a nonflat quotient commutes with individual cohomology groups.

source.place: paragraph 2: explicit projective-line trace and Kummer class under coefficient reduction

proof.text:
For the affine line, the trace is $t_q$ after the open-extension counit into the projective-line compactification [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]. The open scalar comparison preserves this counit: on the open it is the same scalar tensor map and counit identity, while the source is zero off the open; the open adjunction uniquely determines the map. Step 9 therefore proves scalar compatibility for that trace. The composition identity of [lem-pur-etale-compact-scalar-coherence] and the ordered composite-counit formula [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] propagate the equality through each coordinate of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]; rank zero starts with the identity. For a bundle, [def-amb-vector-integration] gives these coordinate traces on every trivializing open. Under $q$ and Step 7's line comparison, both scalar traces have source isomorphic to $Q(A_B[0])=A'_B[0]$, because the original trace is an isomorphism. Both targets are $A'_B[0]$. Thus [lem-pur-degree-zero-derived-map-gluing] applies to the resulting global derived maps and yields
$$t_{\pi,A'}\circ\widetilde q_{\pi,W}=u_B\circ Q_B(t_{\pi,A}),$$
where $l:Q_EW\cong W'$ is Step 7's scalar line map, $\widetilde q_{\pi,W}=R\pi_{!,A'}(l)\circ q_{\pi,W}$ and $u_B:Q_B(A_B[0])\cong A'_B[0]$ is the normalized scalar unit. The open-restriction clause of [lem-pur-etale-compact-scalar-coherence] identifies $q$ restricted to each $U_i$ with the comparison for $E|_{U_i}\to U_i$ and its restricted compactification, and its refinement clause passes to the coordinate-tower compactification. So the local equations compare the actual maps.

source.place: paragraph 2: ordered affine-space traces and sheaf gluing under finite reduction

proof.text:
The projection square of [lem-pur-etale-compact-scalar-coherence], Step 10's trace equality, and the source identification of Step 7 give the exact equation
$$Q_B(c_{\pi,A,K})\,q_{\pi,G_{0,A}K}^{-1}=c_{\pi,A',Q_BK}\,R\pi_{!,A'}(a_{{\rm scalar},K}).$$
Both sides have source $R\pi_{!,A'}Q_EG_{0,A}K$ and target $Q_BK$. By naturality of $q$ and Step 8's defining counit formula for $b$, the transpose of $b_K Q_E(\gamma_{\pi,A,K})$ is the left side. The transpose of $\gamma_{\pi,A',Q_BK}a_{{\rm scalar},K}$ is the right side, by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Consequently
$$b_K Q_E(\gamma_{\pi,A,K})=\gamma_{\pi,A',Q_BK}a_{{\rm scalar},K}.$$
The scalar functor preserves isomorphisms, Step 1 makes both gamma maps invertible, and Step 7 makes $a_{\rm scalar}$ invertible. Solving this equation gives invertibility of $b_K$. This applies to every stated $K$ and to the coefficient-unit OBJECT, where all scalar/single identifications were checked in Step 7. It proves exactly [def-pur-vector-purity-finite-reduction]; taking inverses gives the compatibility for $\alpha$. No exceptional coefficient comparison restricted to prime-power scalar rings or to separated bases has been applied to ramified $A_{E,n}$.

source.place: paragraph 2: transpose the scalar-compatible integration and projection; deduce mate invertibility

proof.text: Set $K=A_B$ in Step 1. Exact coefficient pullback preserves the unit, so the inverse of $\gamma_{\pi,A_B}$ is $\omega_\pi\cong A_E(r)[2r]$, with the reduction square already supplied by Step 11 at that object. At rank zero the relative symmetric algebra of the zero module is $\mathcal O_B$, so [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section] identifies $E\cong B$; the coordinate trace is the identity by [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]. Its transpose, all composition comparisons and the rank-zero scalar line map above are the identity comparisons. An empty base has only zero sheaves and hence only the unique maps in these formulas; the degree-zero gluing statement includes the empty cover. The current statement explicitly reserves integral, rational and algebraically closed coefficients for the separate transport section, so no limit construction is asserted here.

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $\pi:E\to B$ be a vector bundle of constant rank $r$ with zero
section $z$ [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. For every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(B,\Lambda)$ there is a
canonical isomorphism

$$
R\pi^!K\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;L\pi^*K(r)[2r],

compatible with base change, with direct sums of vector bundles, and
with the adjunctions; in particular

$$
\omega_\pi=R\pi^!\Lambda_B\;\cong\;\Lambda_E(r)[2r],
$$

and the identification is compatible with the finite reduction of the
coefficients.
